question:
(a) Explain the saturation property of nuclear force.
(b) How does this property help in explaining the nearly constant density of nuclei?
(c) Why does a nucleon not interact strongly with all other nucleons in a large nucleus?

options.A:
(a) Saturation means each nucleon interacts strongly only with a limited number of nearby nucleons.
(b) Because nuclear force is short-ranged, adding nucleons increases nuclear size so that volume is roughly proportional to $A$. Since mass is also proportional to $A$, density remains nearly constant.
(c) A nucleon does not strongly interact with distant nucleons because nuclear force becomes negligible beyond a few femtometres.
options.B:
(a) Saturation means each nucleon interacts equally with every nucleon in the nucleus.
(b) Therefore density increases linearly with $A$.
(c) A nucleon interacts strongly with all nucleons because nuclear force is long-ranged.
options.C:
(a) Saturation means nuclear force acts only between protons.
(b) Density is zero in large nuclei.
(c) A nucleon does not interact because nuclear force is repulsive.
options.D:
(a) Saturation means nuclear force does not depend on separation.
(b) Nuclear mass is independent of $A$.
(c) A nucleon interacts only with electrons.
